question.text: Will Lebanon's cabinet refer the Dahr al-Baidar explosives case to the Judicial Council before November 28, 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if Lebanon's Council of Ministers (the cabinet) decides to refer the Dahr al-Baidar explosives case to Lebanon's Judicial Council at any time before November 28, 2026 (Beirut time), as reported by [Naharnet's Lebanon news section](https://www.naharnet.com/lebanon) or other [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions). The Dahr al-Baidar case must itself be among the files referred; a decision that refers it together with other files (for example the explosives seized at al-Qasr) counts. A cabinet approval to refer counts even if it is taken in principle or the formal referral decree is issued only later, including where the decision is relayed in the post-session briefing by Lebanon's information minister. The question resolves No if no such cabinet decision is reported before November 28, 2026, including if the cabinet meets without deciding to refer the case or does not meet at all; only a decision by the cabinet counts, not a referral or transfer by any other authority such as the military judiciary or the Ministry of Justice acting alone.
question.fine_print: "Judicial Council" means Lebanon's Judicial Council (al-Majlis al-'Adli), the country's highest criminal court, which hears cases involving state security. A cabinet decision to postpone, defer or withdraw the referral request is not a decision to refer and resolves this question No. A cabinet session held on November 27, 2026 counts even if reporting of its decisions is published after that date.

research:
I found no report that the cabinet has referred the Dahr al-Baidar case to the Judicial Council, and no scheduled session with the file on its agenda. Nothing settles the question yet.

## 4. Base rates
- Since October 22, the item has been on the agenda once and then kept off sessions on October 29, November 5 (postponed) and November 13. Two earlier promises of a session "within two weeks" (from Salam and Nassar) were not kept. So 0 of about 3 or 4 opportunities produced a referral.
- Historically, Lebanese cabinets have referred politically sensitive cases to the Judicial Council slowly or not at all when the Shiite duo (Amal and Hezbollah) objected. The 2021 Tayouneh clashes are an example, and in 2020 the Beirut port blast was referred only after a broad consensus. I found no systematic count of such referrals.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market on this question. The markets you supplied (Lebanon elections, Israel-Lebanon) do not match it.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Possible cabinet sessions around November 19-20 and November 26-27. Agendas are usually published only one or two days ahead, so watch NNA and Naharnet for agenda announcements.
- Whether Aoun and Salam actually put the item on an agenda, and whether a vote is called or deferred again. Berri and Hezbollah oppose the referral, and the judicial source says the votes are not there.
- The military judiciary's progress: indictment by investigating judge Ghada Abu Alwan. The October 22 formula tied a decision to the investigation being completed.
- November 22 is Independence Day, a holiday that may shift the session schedule.
- Escalation in the LF boycott, or Kataeb pressure ([Elsiyasa](https://elsiyasa.com/article/434321)).

Sources I could not open: IMLebanon (403) and L'Orient Today (403). L'Orient reported Aoun saying a session would be devoted to the issue "within two weeks", but I could not confirm the date of that article.

forecasts.reasoning:
**(a) Time left and what Yes requires.** About 11 days remain, with roughly two possible cabinet sessions (around Nov 19-20 and Nov 26-27). Independence Day on Nov 22 may disrupt the schedule. Yes requires the Council of Ministers to decide, even in principle, to refer the Dahr al-Baidar case to the Judicial Council, with the decision reported by credible sources.

**(b) Status quo.** No referral. The request has been pending since the Oct 22 postponement "until investigations are completed," and the file has been kept off every session since.

**(c) Base rate.** My reference class is contested Judicial Council referrals that the Shiite duo opposes. These are rarely approved quickly, and past referrals usually came through consensus. The item has missed 3-4 opportunities since Oct 22, and two promises of a session "within two weeks" lapsed. A per-session hazard of about 5-10% across two sessions gives a base rate of roughly 10-15%.

**(d) Strongest evidence.**
- **For Yes:**
  - Nov 13: MTV reported that Aoun and Salam concluded the item should "soon" go on a cabinet agenda.
  - Nov 13: Justice Minister Nassar said he hoped it would be on the next session's agenda.
  - Nov 13: An-Nahar reportedly mentioned a vote "at next week's session."
  - Nov 15: A Lebanon24 sidebar mentioned the item being on Thursday's agenda.
  - The LF boycott keeps up pressure on the government.
- **For No:**
  - Nov 15: A Lebanon24 senior judicial source cited a "presidential understanding" against referral and said a vote would win only 5 votes. The source added that a failed vote would damage the cover for the August decisions, so the item should not come to cabinet at all.
  - Nov 3: Al Jadeed's security source said there would be "no referral."
  - Al-Jareeda and Elsiyasa reported a settlement among the presidents to keep the file with the military judiciary.
  - Berri and Hezbollah strongly oppose the referral, and Qassem has hardened his line.
  - MTV is LF-leaning, so its report may overstate the momentum.
